subject: pufferfish
pitch: A startled pufferfish fully puffed up into a ball. Creamy yellow skin with brown leopard spots on top fading to a white belly, short spikes all over, a tiny pouting mouth, big worried round eyes, small fluttering side fins and a stubby fan-shaped tail. A few bubbles rise from its mouth.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a pufferfish model as a three.js module, orienting it to face +Z with its lowest spikes touching the floor at y=0, and deciding whether it needs any base structure or can just rest as a sphere shape.

For sizing, I'm scaling toward a realistic puffed pufferfish body around 0.22m radius with small spikes, and planning to compute a bounding box afterward to shift the whole group so its lowest point lands exactly at y=0, regardless of bubble elements above. I'm sketching the body as a slightly irregular sphere with low-poly faceting for a spiky, puffed look.

For the surface coloring, I'm designing a canvas texture mapped onto the sphere: a vertical gradient from creamy yellow at the top to white on the belly, with irregular leopard-style spots scattered across the upper portion. Since UV mapping pinches spots near the poles, I'm compensating by widening spot size based on latitude so they don't look squeezed, and considering whether to also add a few physical 3D spot discs for texture depth alongside the painted canvas pattern.

I should guard the canvas texture creation so it fails gracefully if document isn't available, falling back to a plain material color. I'm also working out the exact UV-to-direction mapping for three.js's SphereGeometry so I can correctly place spots: tracing how u maps to longitude (u=0.25 is +Z, u=0.5 is +X, etc.) and how v maps to latitude from top to bottom.

Converting this back the other way, I derive that for a world direction, phi = atan2(dz, -dx) gives u, and acos(dy)/π gives v for the canvas lookup. I'm settling on a low-poly sphere (around 24x16 segments) with flat shading plus a spot texture, then planning to scatter short cone-shaped spikes across the surface using Fibonacci sphere distribution for even spacing.

For the spikes themselves, I'll use around 150 individual low-poly cones sharing geometry/material rather than an instanced mesh, to stay safely under any mesh-count limits. I'm thinking of coloring them cream-yellow with slightly darker tips on top and white on the belly, possibly using a few material variants based on height.

For orientation, each spike cone needs its axis rotated from its default +Y direction to point outward along the fish's surface normal, with its position offset outward from the body radius. I'll also need to carve out exclusion zones so spikes don't spawn over the eyes, mouth, fin bases, or tail.

For the body itself, I'm settling on an ellipsoid shape (slightly different radii per axis) rather than a perfect sphere, with surface points and normals computed by scaling the direction vector by those radii -- this keeps things simple while giving a rounder puffed-up look without needing complex vertex deformation.

For the face, I'm placing a tiny pouting mouth near the front-bottom, and positioning big round worried eyes toward the front-sides of the body. Each eye will be layered: a white socket sphere, then a golden-teal iris disc, a small startled black pupil, and a white highlight dot, with slanted brow pieces above tilted so the inner corners sit higher for that worried expression.

I'm thinking through how to tilt the eyelid cap geometry so it droops on the outer corner while lifting at the inner corner, matching that classic worried-brow slant by rotating the cap's axis toward the outward direction.
